topic.title: Safety Alignment Mechanisms and Robustness to Fine-Tuning
topic.overview: Safety alignment seeks to shape model responses, but the resulting behavior can change under fine-tuning, prompting, or architectural modifications. This topic investigates harmful-output evaluation, mechanisms associated with alignment, and methods for preserving or deepening safety behavior. It distinguishes measured compliance from stronger claims about general understanding or robustness.
topic.whyItMatters: A safety score is only as informative as the situations and harms it measures. Models may retain task capabilities while losing protective behavior, so adaptation needs evaluation that probes both. Mechanistic observations can guide interventions, but findings on selected models and attacks require validation before broad generalization.
topic.evolution: A 2022 paper analyzes dimensions of harmful text for benchmark design. Studies in 2024 examine fine-tuning risks and parameter-space safety landscapes. Later representatives explore safety-preserving updates and pretraining; a 2026 verification-based framework trains reasoning models to critique response safety and tests transfer to unfamiliar jailbreak settings.
openQuestions: Which evaluations predict safety failures after benign downstream fine-tuning?
How can verification training improve response safety without merely learning evaluator-specific patterns?

papers.title: Towards Context-Invariant Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: AIR uses verifiable prompts as fixed anchors to improve alignment consistency across differently framed requests.

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating Token-Pruning-Induced Vulnerabilities in VLMs
papers.tldr: Safety-Aware Pruning counteracts attention concentration on malicious visual tokens, reducing pruning-related attack success without reported efficiency or utility losses.

papers.title: Who Transfers Safety? Identifying and Targeting Cross-Lingual Shared Safety Neurons
papers.tldr: Targeting a small set of shared safety neurons improves safety across non-high-resource languages while preserving general model capabilities.
